# External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes — concept pack

> Source-anchored research for External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes. Run status: COMPLETED.

## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes (11/1)

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB documents an in-place transfer of the existing AppDB StatefulSet and its persistent storage to a MongoDB resource, without copying or recreating AppDB data. The MCK 1.12.0 release notes describe the same mechanism. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongodb-kubernetes/releases
- [statement] During this migration, spec.applicationDatabase.passwordSecretKeyRef is unsupported: the operator generates a new password and rotates any supplied password. Treat credential rotation as a migration effect even when the data volumes are retained. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/om-appdb-backup.md

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Create a MongoDB resource named exactly <primary-om-name>-db with spec.role: AppDB before adding the Ops Manager external reference. Its ownership-related Pending phase is expected until spec.externalApplicationDatabaseRef triggers release of the existing StatefulSet. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes

## Facts and statements

- [statement] On forward migration the operator removes the Ops Manager owner reference and marks the StatefulSet ready for adoption. The coordination annotation is mongodb.com/appdb-migration-ready; the operator sets and reads it, and administrators must not set it manually. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/om-appdb-backup.md
- [statement] Verify completion by checking that StatefulSet metadata.ownerReferences changes from MongoDBOpsManager/<primary-om-name> to MongoDB/<primary-om-name>-db, the MongoDB and Ops Manager phases reach Running, and Ops Manager status.applicationDatabase.phase becomes Disabled. Disabled means internal AppDB management stopped. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes
- [statement] Preserving Ops Manager pod uptime depends on preserving its computed AppDB connection string and hostnames. The migration procedure supports the default replica-set port; non-default ports are unsupported. If AppDB pod templates or container sets differ, AppDB itself can be unavailable for one to two minutes even though the ownership transfer retains its data. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes
- [statement] Interpret the documented PV ownership transfer as a management handoff, not proof that cluster-scoped PV metadata.ownerReferences now points to the namespaced MongoDB resource. Kubernetes permits cluster-scoped dependents to reference only cluster-scoped owners; the AppDB procedure demonstrates the owner-reference change on the StatefulSet. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes · also: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/owners-dependents/
- [statement] After the target resource is waiting, patch the primary Ops Manager resource with spec.externalApplicationDatabaseRef pointing to it using kind: MongoDB. This forward procedure does not require deleting either custom resource or the StatefulSet. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes
- [statement] Once spec.externalApplicationDatabaseRef is set, spec.applicationDatabase no longer controls an internal AppDB for that Ops Manager resource. The migration patch may remove spec.applicationDatabase, but leaving it present has no effect. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes
- [statement] Before forward migration, match the target MongoDB resource version to the running internal AppDB and select a version offered by the management Ops Manager. MongoDB does not automatically reconcile the external resource configuration with the internal AppDB configuration; the user must specify equivalent settings. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/om-appdb-backup.md
- [statement] Do not substitute PVC deletion and rebinding for the documented ownership handoff. The forward procedure keeps the existing data in place; Red Hat documents that a Delete reclaim policy removes both the PV object and its backing storage asset after release, whereas Retain supports manual reclamation. Retained data in this migration is not evidence that the operator changes persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy to Retain. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/migrate-appdb-to-external.md · keywords: External AppDB resource ownership migration with retained volumes · also: https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.21/html/storage/understanding-persistent-storage
